mainEntity.name: Is AI newsletter drafting suitable if I am not an expert on the topic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use AI to support your expertise, not to disguise a lack of understanding. For technical or unfamiliar subjects, first ask for a plain-language explanation, source map, disputed points, and questions an expert should resolve; then decide whether the topic is ready for publication. Run My AI Biz serves readers who want approachable explanations, so clarity matters, but simplification must not remove important limits. Identify claims that could affect purchasing, security, business operations, or expected results. Have a knowledgeable person review those sections before sending. If evidence remains weak, publish a clearly labeled exploratory issue or choose a better-supported topic.
acceptedAnswer.description: It can help you learn and organize a topic, but it should not replace subject knowledge or review. Ask for primary sources, disputed points, limitations, and unresolved questions before drafting. For Run My AI Biz topics involving AI tools or business workflows, verify capabilities and pricing directly and avoid presenting experiments as proven outcomes.
